_about: Every word and number on herrada.me. scripts/build.py writes index.html, how-i-build.html and 404.html from this file and the templates in src/. Text values are HTML fragments. {n:key} prints a count, {over:key} prints the largest multiple of 50 below a count, for copy that says more than, {read:key} prints a count's read date and {date:YYYY-MM-DD} prints a date. Every count carries the date it was read and where it was read from. After an edit, run `python3 scripts/build.py` and commit the pages with this file. `make ci` fails when they differ.

about.body: I'm Luis, a software engineer in Monterrey, Mexico. I have spent 18+ years taking products from the first idea to production, and I still like the simple solution best. Today I build Rentaventa, a real-estate platform for the city's brokers, with a partner. I also build Smithy, the workshop where AI agents do most of my building and I keep the decisions. The rest is for the love of it: an archive of Mexico's trees, a vim trainer, chess on a real board, a box of tiny games.

body: From 2016 to 2019 I ran Vordem, a digital product agency. Its home page had a heading I still work by: “A balanced approach.” Strategists, developers, designers and product managers on one problem, looking for the simple answer. Today agents hold most of those seats, and the decisions stay with me.

I work in a terminal: i3, tmux, vim. Every project I own has one command that has to pass before anything ships, and a written record of why things are the way they are. That holds for the real-estate platform and for the tiny games.
rules: One command gates every repo. Nothing ships that does not pass.
I write down why. More than {over:adrs_all} decision records across seven projects, ten of them for thirteen tiny games.
Status is stated as it is. Pre-launch means pre-launch.
Machines check the work. Every vim puzzle is replayed in CI. Every game is replayed from a seed.

how_i_build.title: How I build with agents
how_i_build.description: How Luis Herrada builds software with AI agents: Smithy, a personal system where agents do the building and he keeps the decisions.
sub: Smithy · in daily use since October 2026

idea.kind: one person, many agents, one record
idea.lead: AI agents can write code faster than one person can follow. Smithy is my answer: a personal system where agents do the building and I can still see the design, the decisions and the state of everything.

body: In 2016 I started an agency called Vordem. Its home page put our way of working under one heading, “A balanced approach”: strategists, developers, designers and product managers on the same problem, looking for a simple and elegant answer. We were ten people and shipped 10+ products.

The workshop I run today works the same way, with agents in most of the seats. One shapes an idea into a work item with me. One argues with the design before any code exists. One builds. A panel of reviewers checks correctness, security, QA and UX from the diff and the evidence, and never sees the plan. The decisions stay with me.

seats.now: An agent and I shape an idea into a work item with a problem, context, acceptance criteria and a test plan.
Bigger items get a written design, and an agent argues with it before any code exists.
The smiths. Each claims an item, works in its own copy of the repo and opens a pull request.
A board that moves only on facts, and one list of what needs me.

board.kind: the life of a work item
body: A card moves only when something real happens: a claim, a gate verdict, a pull request marked ready, a merge, a deploy, an answer. There is no command to move a card.
Needs input is a flag over any column. It is raised only for a blocker, a design decision, a destructive action or a question of intent.

An item leaves grooming only when its definition is complete for its size: a problem, context and acceptance criteria, then a design, a test plan and risks for bigger items, plus a diagram and a design review for the biggest.
board.caption: The level map: eight columns, a held lane for my pick, and nine real work items, where they stood on {date:2026-11-25}.

Phones and touch: a desktop-keyboard notice in the player, a status bar that never clips.
Keyboard flow: Enter and r after a solve, ex commands for reset, skip, give up and quit.

loop.intro: Every work item plays the same eight levels, in this order. Each picture below is one still frame.

levels.name: Shape
levels.text: An idea becomes a work item with a problem, context, acceptance criteria and a test plan. Its mode is set here: autonomous or review.
levels.alt: An idea in a dashed box, an arrow, and a work item with four filled lines and a mode chip.

levels.name: Review the design
levels.text: Bigger items get a written design and an adversarial review before any code exists.
levels.alt: A written design stands between two agents. The one on the right has left three red marks on it.

levels.name: Build
levels.text: An agent claims the item, works in its own copy of the repo and opens a pull request.
levels.alt: A branch leaves the main line. An agent stands at its tip after three commits, and a dashed line points back to the main line.

levels.name: Pass the gates
levels.text: make ci on the exact commit. A gauntlet of reviewers for correctness, security, QA and UX, who see the diff and the evidence and never the plan. An end-to-end run against a real local stack. Each gate leaves a stamp: a verdict tied to a commit.
levels.note: Gates: ci, review, qa, design-review, deploy. Verdicts: pass, pass with notes, blocked, needs human, skipped, error.
levels.alt: A card under the third of three gates. It carries two stamps and a third is coming down.

levels.name: Land
levels.text: An autonomous item merges and deploys when every stamp is green, and leaves a summary to read later. A review item stops at a ready pull request and waits for me.
levels.alt: A stamped card at a fork. One path climbs to a platform with a flag. The other stops at a red bar in front of a person.

levels.name: Ask only what matters
levels.text: Critical questions arrive with options, a recommended answer, the cost to reverse and what happens if I do nothing. The agent then moves to other work. Every other judgment call is made, logged with its reason and reviewed later.
levels.alt: One question in a short list, with two options and one of them marked. The agent has already moved on to another card.

levels.name: Learn
levels.text: On a fixed rhythm each session turns what it learned into a skill, a note or a new work item.
levels.alt: Five tools hang on a wall. The newest is yellow, and the agent that made it stands under it.

levels.name: Pace
levels.text: A governor starts new runs only when there is headroom, so a long night of work never hits a wall.
levels.alt: A meter with six of ten slots filled. Three agents run in their lanes and a fourth waits behind a yellow bar.

how_i_build.after: Calls feed the record. After a call with my partner an agent writes the notes and files the action items.

paragraphs: VP-0010, “Copy fix: stop promising a daily set until one exists”. The vim-puzzles dashboard still said “Daily vim puzzles” after the daily set was gone. An agent found the gap while grooming the app's backlog: the new About page would have repeated a promise the product no longer kept.
It raised one question for me, with two options and a recommended answer. I had told the agents not to get blocked, so the recommended answer was taken and logged for me to read.

Thirteen minutes later the fix was built and had passed CI. Fourteen minutes after that it had passed review. It was deployed four and a half hours after the decision. The line it left on the dashboard is the app's line today: “Vim puzzles, scored against par.”
before: Groomed the same day. Its definition is complete: a small item, copy only, gates ci and review, one question open. Column: Backlog
Decided, {date:2026-10-20}: the recommended answer, drop the promise. The item is ranked. Column: Next up

splits.name: built
splits.note: Claimed and built. A branch and a pull request. ci: pass Column: In dev

splits.name: reviewed
splits.note: review: pass Column: In code review

story.close: The card visits seven of the eight columns. It never stops in In QA: a copy fix has no QA gate. Dates are UTC.

rules.kind: twelve decisions from the ledger, shortened
items: Record decisions as short records. Bodies never change. A new record supersedes an old one.
Convention over configuration: the standard make targets are the contract with every project.
An item's mode is set at grooming: autonomous items land and deploy when green, review items wait for me.
The window is a viewer. Every change goes through a session and the API.
Every working session turns its lessons into skills.
Gated pull requests land by default.
Nothing waits for me unless it is destructive.
Everything that waits on me lives in one list.
Pace the agents with a governor.
Calls feed the record: each transcript becomes a summary and work items.

close.lead: Smithy is its own first project: it was built with itself from the first day. This site is on the board too.
